what: WP2021 converted to attribution fixtures: a Chinese corpus whose gold is a CHARACTER

corpus.name: WP2021 / World of Plainness
corpus.licence: none stated; fetched and converted locally, never committed

why_it_matters: every method result in GOALS.md comes from four Japanese light novels IN TRANSLATION; nothing has been validated on non-English prose. Goal 1.3 is the document's largest known overstatement. This is a corpus where the gold is a canonical character with alias groups and gender, unlike RiQuA whose golds are unresolved mention spans (39.4% bare pronouns).
not_an_addressee_corpus: WP2021 has NO addressee field and cannot test addressee_confusion.py. That needs PDNC, RiQuA, or the Japanese BCCWJ annotation.
format_consistency_note: all five properties hold on every instance. They are asserted on every build, not assumed: an earlier reader of the SQuAD-shaped re-release GUESSED the field meanings, ran clean, passed 14 tests and reported 99.8% resolved, but agreed with the quote's own named speaker only 11.6% of the time. A passing test does not ask whether the format assumption holds.
released_splits_are_smaller_than_the_pap: the paper reports 2,548 quotes in the final dataset; the released train/dev/test files contain 1,835 instances. Verified not to be a parser bug: strict, loose and any-bracket counts of block markers all agree at 1,835. Recorded as an observation, unexplained.
